Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, credit supply conditions around the time of the June 15, 2022 FOMC decision were more supportive than the Financial Stability Report alone implies: banks eased C&I loan standards and reduced credit line costs, with stronger business loan demand tied to inventory, accounts receivable, plant, and equipment; multifamily standards eased, while construction and other CRE standards were largely unchanged. On the consumer side, standards eased for credit cards, demand was stronger for HELOCs and autos, but weaker for RRE. While foreign banks reported tighter C&I standards, the domestic SLOOS picture suggests credit was still flowing, partially offsetting the growth drag from a 75 bp hike and balance-sheet runoff. Net: still a hawkish, tightening-driven negative for near-term activity and financial conditions, but less negative once SLOOS resilience is factored in.
